method: Visual hypotheses + representative manufacturer ratings at DT50. User authorized photo estimates; not measurements or product identification.

charleston.title: Zehnder Charleston technical datasheet, horizontal table p1
charleston.basis: Representative painted steel columns, not an identified brand. Per-section outputs derived from listed section counts; nominal section pitch 46 mm.

charleston-mtm.title: Zehnder Charleston made-to-measure, July 2023, per-section table
charleston-mtm.basis: Representative 900/1000 mm per-section output only; no prices imported. Exponent 1.3 assumed for these rows.

compact.title: Stelrad Compact technical specification, W/m at 75/65/20°C
compact.basis: Representative steel panel outputs per metre and published n coefficients; not product identification.

nobis.title: Zehnder Nobis NOB-100-050 technical datasheet p1
nobis.basis: 965 x 500 mm chrome brass frame, 210 W at DT50, n=1.28. Used only as an analogue for the brass-looking bathroom frame.

emitters.title: Lower-ground column radiator
emitters.observation: About eight front sections are visible on the exposed brick wall. Bottom is cropped.
emitters.assumptions: Central guess: 8 sections, about 900 mm high, 3 columns deep (~394 mm wide). Compare 7–9 sections, 750–1000 mm, 2–4 columns. Brick/door scale is approximate; study assignment follows the earlier tentative lower-ground attribution.

emitters.title: Hall column radiator
emitters.observation: White tubular sections are visible; near end and lower edge extend beyond the photo.
emitters.assumptions: Central guess: 18 sections, 600 mm high, 3 columns (~854 mm wide). Plausible alternatives: 14 sections/600 mm/2 columns to 24 sections/750 mm/4 columns. Cropping limits the total count.

emitters.title: Living-room bay radiator
emitters.observation: A separate white column radiator is visible below the central bay window, behind the table and chair.
emitters.assumptions: Central guess: 24 sections, 600 mm high, 3 columns (~1130 mm wide), using the window span as a loose scale cue. Occlusion allows 20 sections/500 mm/2 columns to 30 sections/600 mm/4 columns. Dining photo is a repeat view, not another emitter.

emitters.title: Kitchen window radiator
emitters.observation: A narrow part of a white ribbed radiator is visible behind the table/chair below the window.
emitters.assumptions: Very weak dimensions: central panel hypothesis 600 x 600 mm, K1; alternatives 450 x 400 mm K1 to 600 x 800 mm K2. Panel versus tubular construction cannot be resolved; this is a broad output proxy. The second kitchen photo shows the same position.

emitters.title: Rear living-area panel radiator
emitters.observation: White ribbed panel below the side window, largely hidden by the chair and table; separate from the kitchen-window radiator.
emitters.assumptions: Central guess: 450 x 1000 mm K1. Compare 450 x 700 mm K1 to 600 x 1200 mm K2; width uses the window as an approximate reference. Rear photograph has no metric camera calibration for emitter sizing.

emitters.title: Front-bedroom bay radiator
emitters.observation: White tubular radiator beneath the central bay window, partly hidden by the chair.
emitters.assumptions: Front bay identifies Bedroom 1 more strongly than the listing caption alone. Central guess: 28 sections, 600 mm high, 3 columns (~1314 mm wide). Compare 22 sections/500 mm/2 columns to 32 sections/600 mm/4 columns.

emitters.title: Bathroom towel frame
emitters.observation: Brass-coloured open frame with a few horizontal rails and apparent valve connections, above the bath.
emitters.assumptions: Approximate 800 x 500 mm frame. Central 180 W DT50, bracket 120–300 W, using a 210 W 965 x 500 mm brass-frame analogue. Multipliers allow different dimensions/finish; this is a heuristic, not validated geometric scaling. Hot-water/electric connection and towel effects need checking.

emitters.title: Unassigned bedroom radiator
emitters.observation: White column radiator below a sash window beside the bed.
emitters.assumptions: Central guess: 14 sections/600 mm/3 columns (~670 mm wide). Compare 10 sections/500 mm/2 columns to 20 sections/750 mm/4 columns. Sloping ceiling suggests the rear bedroom, but attribution to Bedroom 2 versus 3 is unresolved; exclude from room totals.

unresolved.observation: Possible radiator behind the right-hand sofa, but upholstery and emitter edges are not reliably separable. Retain the original observation; no numeric estimate and no double counting with the bay radiator.

limits: Section counts run across the radiator; column counts describe front-to-back depth. Never confuse them.
All sizes are photo guesses. Source pixels are not metric measurements and are not independently rectified.
Photo inventories are partial. A shortfall for visible radiators cannot prove that the entire room requires replacements.
Manufacturer curves are analogues; the actual installed brands/models and hydronic connection remain unverified.
Photos with no visible emitter remain unknown; bathroom mirror reflections and repeat room views are not additional emitters.
